research.region: Europe/CIS (UKR, ROU focus) + MENA + LAC + high-income sweep
research.summary: Across Europe, the CIS, MENA, Latin America and the high-income world, the tubewell/borehole JMP category is overwhelmingly motorized (grid-electric), unlike sub-Saharan Africa. No census or MICS/DHS in this region splits the borehole category into hand vs motorized directly except Bosnia 2013 (electric hydrophore wells outnumber manual wells ~11:1, i.e. ~8% handpump share), which serves as the best regional anchor. Ukraine's MICS 2012 puts tubewell/borehole at 5.9% of households (dug 'kolodyaz' wells, 21.5%, are a separate excluded category); Ukrainian boreholes ('svyerdlovyna') are typified by electric submersible/hydrophore setups, and war reporting (UNICEF/IOM) repeatedly documents that power outages disable borehole pumps, with solar retrofits now being installed — direct evidence of electric dependence — though village hand-pump columns and shallow Abyssinian driven wells keep a 5-20% rural handpump share plausible. Romania's rural self-supply standard is the drilled 'foraj' with a hidrofor (electric pressure set); the traditional manual fântână is a dug well outside the borehole category, so Romania's handpump share among borehole users is very low (0-10% rural). High-income countries are confirmed near-100% motorized: US EPA counts >23M households (~43M people) on private wells, all on electric submersible/jet pumps; Nordic private supply is drilled bedrock boreholes far beyond handpump suction depth; France, Austria, NZ the same. Iran is mostly rural-piped (87.7%) with electric boreholes, but ~37,000 operational gravity-fed qanats are a genuine zero-power resilience pocket. The exceptions with high handpump shares are Haiti (NGO handpump boreholes, almost no rural grid: 60-90%), lowland Central Asia (Karakalpakstan/Khorezm/Dashoguz hand pumps still a main non-piped source: 20-60%), and to a lesser degree Nicaragua, where a 2022 resurvey found 80% of original rope pumps already replaced by small electric centrifugal pumps (10-40% remaining). Regional default for uncovered countries: urban 0-5%, rural 2-15% handpump share among borehole users, with motorized pumping essentially all grid-electric (diesel backup marginal, solar growing only in war/off-grid niches).

findings.source: Ukraine MICS 2012 (WS1, State Statistics Service/UNICEF, via World Bank Microdata catalog 2348) + UNICEF/IOM war reporting 2022-2024 + Bosnia 2013 census analogue
findings.quote: MICS 2012 WS1: 'Tube well, Borehole' = 663 cases = 5.9% of households; 'Protected well' (kolodyaz, dug, bucket) = 2,432 = 21.5% (separate JMP category, excluded); piped into dwelling 59.7%. MICS gives NO hand/motorized split within the borehole row. Split estimated: Bosnia 2013 census analogue gives manual/(manual+electric) = 1.1/(1.1+12.2) = 8.3%; adjusted upward for Ukraine's shallow Abyssinian driven wells with hand pumps and village hand-pump columns (kachalky) in high-water-table oblasts -> 5-20%. Electric dependence directly evidenced by war reporting: 'shelling often caused power outages, disabling the pumps' (UNICEF, eastern Ukraine villages); IOM 2024 provided solar stations to power community boreholes in Mykolaiv region.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Motorized share is nearly all grid-electric (submersible or surface hydrophore sets). Diesel generators appear only as war-time backup at utility wellfields; solar pump retrofits are a growing war-response niche (IOM/UNICEF installs since 2023). Pre-war baseline: assume ~95%+ of motorized is grid.
findings.caveats: 11.5M model borehole users vs MICS 5.9% of households implies the model category also absorbs communal artesian boreholes and post-2012 private drilling growth; no post-2012 national survey splits pump type. Survey is pre-2014, flagged for drift: private borehole drilling boomed after 2012, which pushes the electric share UP (new boreholes are deep + submersible).

findings.source: Ukraine MICS 2012 + typology of urban private-sector housing boreholes
findings.quote: Urban borehole users are households in private-sector (odnoosobova zabudova) city districts and suburbs with own drilled wells; these are deep drilled wells with electric submersible pumps + hydrophore tanks as standard practice. Hand-pump street columns are a village phenomenon. No direct urban split exists; bounded 0-5%.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric ~100% of motorized. Kyiv's ~300-400 public artesian 'buvety' are deep boreholes with electric pumps (fail in blackout).
findings.caveats: Analogue/typology reasoning, not a measured split.

findings.source: INS Romania (74.1% of resident population connected to public water supply, 2021) + rural groundwater case studies (MDPI Sustainability 17:6530 Ceanu Mare; Water 17:2758) + market typology of 'foraj + hidrofor'
findings.quote: INS 2021: 74.1% of Romania's resident population connected to the public water supply network; the rural remainder self-supplies. Romanian rural self-supply splits into (a) traditional 'fantana' = DUG well with bucket/windlass -> JMP dug-well category, EXCLUDED from the borehole denominator, and (b) 'foraj'/'put forat' = drilled borehole, which is drilled precisely to feed an in-house pressurized system and is fitted with an electric hidrofor (pressure pump set) as the standard, near-universal configuration. Hand pumps mounted on drilled wells are a rare budget/backup option. Hence handpump/(handpump+motorized borehole) = 0-10% rural.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Essentially 100% grid-electric (rural electrification ~100%); diesel/solar household pumping negligible.
findings.caveats: The model's 4.3M ROU borehole users likely maps census 'own system' (sistem propriu) households; if any dug-well-with-electric-pump households are inside that number they are still electric, so the motorized conclusion is robust. No census table splits pump type directly.

findings.source: Same as rural; urban periphery self-supply is foraj+hidrofor by construction
findings.quote: Urban borehole users are peri-urban houses with drilled wells feeding indoor plumbing via electric hidrofor; a hand pump cannot pressurize indoor plumbing, so the configuration is electric by definition. 0-3%.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric ~100%.
findings.caveats: Typology reasoning.

findings.source: BiH Census of Population, Households and Dwellings 2013, dwelling water-supply table (seed evidence from prior phase, retained)
findings.quote: Census 2013: dwellings with own water supply via 'hydrophore' (electric pressure pump) wells = 12.2% of households vs simple dug/drilled/artesian wells without powered pump ~1.1%. Handpump/manual share among self-supply well users = 1.1/(1.1+12.2) = 8.3%; bound 5-12%.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric; no diesel/solar household pumping tradition.
findings.caveats: The manual 1.1% includes some dug wells (bucket), so 8.3% is an UPPER-leaning estimate for the borehole-only category. This is the only direct census split found in the whole region and anchors the regional default.

findings.source: Moldova MICS 2012 WS1 (via World Bank Microdata) + APASAN village survey typology
findings.quote: MICS 2012 WS1: tube well/borehole = 68 cases = 0.6% of households; protected well (dug, bucket - excluded) = 25.3%; piped into dwelling 44.9%. Moldova's non-piped rural water is dominated by dug wells with buckets, NOT boreholes; village artesian boreholes ('sonda arteziana') feed piped mini-networks (counted as piped) and are electric. The tiny residual private borehole group is hydrophore/electric as in Romania/Ukraine; 0-15% handpump.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric; artesian village systems are electric tower systems.
findings.caveats: Borehole user population is very small (<0.1M), so this barely moves regional totals.

findings.source: US EPA Private Drinking Water Wells program; USGS domestic supply wells
findings.quote: EPA: 'more than 23 million households rely on private wells for drinking water' (~43M people, ~15% of population). Standard equipment is an electric submersible pump (deep wells) or electric jet pump (shallow); hand pumps are hobby/backup items only. Handpump share as main supply: 0-2% (Amish and off-grid communities are the only material exception).
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric ~99%; small solar/generator niche among off-grid homesteads.
findings.caveats: Confirms prior phase's high-income finding. Public-supply borehole (community wells) users are likewise grid-electric with backup gensets at some utilities.

findings.source: Geological Survey/geoenergy literature: ~80,000 bedrock boreholes for water supply, ~4,000 drilled/yr (Gehlin et al. 2016, Nordic borehole statistics)
findings.quote: 'About 80,000 wells have been drilled in bedrock for groundwater supply in Norway... mostly used as water supply for single houses, farms... ~4,000 new wells drilled annually.' Bedrock boreholes are typically 40-100+ m deep - physically beyond hand-pump suction lift - and are fitted with electric submersible pumps. Handpump share ~0. Applies equally to Sweden (600,000+ registered wells) and Finland ('porakaivo' drilled wells, electric).
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric ~100% (Nordic rural grid is universal).
findings.caveats: Use as the finding for SWE, FIN, DNK, ISL too.

findings.source: French private well/forage declaration regime (puits et forages domestiques, >1M declared) + prior-phase high-income finding; French Guiana seed evidence (36 documented handpumps) retained
findings.quote: Metropolitan France: private 'forages domestiques' are drilled wells with electric pumps (immerged or surface); drinking self-supply is a small population and effectively all electric. Old courtyard hand pumps are ornamental/garden. 0-2%. French Guiana (prior phase): exactly 36 documented 'pompes a motricite humaine' + ~10 treated forages - a rounding error nationally.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric ~100%.
findings.caveats: No census split; typology + regulatory registry reasoning.

findings.source: Austrian Hausbrunnen (household well) literature; ~10% of population on private wells/springs, prior-phase high-income finding
findings.quote: Roughly 700,000-900,000 Austrians self-supply from Hausbrunnen (wells) and springs; wells feeding indoor plumbing use electric pressure sets (Hauswasserwerk). Hand pumps survive as garden/backup fixtures only. 0-3%. Same conclusion for Switzerland/Germany self-supply pockets.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric ~100%; spring users are gravity-fed (resilient) but are a different JMP category.
findings.caveats: Analogue to Nordic/US pattern; no direct census split.

findings.source: NZ self-supply (~10-13% of population on private bores/tanks); prior-phase high-income finding
findings.quote: NZ rural/lifestyle-block bores are drilled wells with electric submersible pumps feeding pressure tanks; hand pumps effectively absent as main supply. 0-2%. (Much NZ self-supply is roof rainwater - a different JMP category - which shrinks the borehole denominator further.)
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric; some solar pumping on remote stations.
findings.caveats: Analogue reasoning.

findings.source: Iran Ministry of Energy/ABFAR rural water coverage; qanat inventories (~37,000-39,000 operational)
findings.quote: Rural drinking water access 87.7% (2022), overwhelmingly via piped village systems fed by electric wells/springs; urban 96.2%. Iran has ~650,000 wells but these are dominated by agricultural abstraction (NOT drinking shares - excluded per pitfall 2). Direct household borehole drinking users are few and use electric pumps (rural electrification ~99.9%). Hand pumps have no tradition in Iran; the human/no-power groundwater is the QANAT (~37,000-39,000 operational, gravity flow), which JMP-wise surfaces as protected spring or piped scheme, not tubewell. Handpump share within the borehole category: 0-10%.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric dominant; diesel pumping common for agriculture and some remote village systems - for the non-HEMP scenario a modest diesel share of village drinking systems (~5-15%) plausibly survives grid loss. Qanat/gravity-spring users are fully resilient but sit outside the borehole category.
findings.caveats: If the model's Iran borehole users actually include qanat-supplied households, the effective 'resilient share' is much higher than the handpump share - flag for the integrator.

findings.source: ADB Western Uzbekistan Water Supply System Development project surveys (RRP UZB 50259, PSA); Uzbekistan MICS 2021-22 (tubewell category exists, no pump split)
findings.quote: ADB PSA survey (Karakalpakstan/Khorezm): 'hand pumps identified as one of the main sources of drinking water in project areas other than piped water'; only 12.9% of Karakalpakstan's rural population connected to centralized supply. Soviet-era hand pumps (kachalka) on shallow driven tubewells remain widespread in the Amu Darya lowlands, while better-off households have converted to small electric pumps. No survey splits the tubewell category -> wide bound 20-60% rural.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Motorized = grid-electric (rural electrification ~100%), though with brownout-prone supply; negligible diesel/solar household pumping.
findings.caveats: MICS 2021-22 WS.1 has the tubewell/borehole denominator by stratum but no pump type. Salinity makes many hand-pump tubewells non-drinking sources in Karakalpakstan - drinking-share may skew lower than pump counts imply (pitfall 3). Urban UZB: use 0-15%.

findings.source: Analogue to Karakalpakstan (same Amu Darya lowland aquifer/settlement pattern, Dashoguz province); Turkmenistan MICS 2019 has tubewell category, no split
findings.quote: Dashoguz and Lebap rural areas share the Karakalpakstan pattern: shallow driven tubewells with Soviet hand pumps alongside growing electric pump ownership. No national survey splits the category; adopt the UZB bound 20-60%.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric (electricity historically free/subsidized - high electric conversion likely); no solar/diesel household niche.
findings.caveats: Pure analogue; small borehole population.

findings.source: MICS 2015 (tubewell/borehole category, no split); rural water program (Ak Bulak) documentation
findings.quote: Kazakh rural boreholes ('skvazhina') are deep (cold climate, deep water tables) and electric-pumped; village hand-pump columns persist in some southern oblasts. No survey split; bound 5-25% rural, lower urban.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric ~100% of motorized.
findings.caveats: Expert bound. Kyrgyzstan/Tajikistan: borehole users are a small slice (piped/standpipe/spring dominate per Tajikistan 'Glass Half Full' 2017 diagnostic); apply the same 5-25% bound with low confidence.

findings.source: Haiti EMMUS-VI (DHS 2016-17) tubewell category + NGO borehole-handpump inventories (Afridev/India MkII standard; e.g. Leogane-Gressier borehole-handpump studies) + rural grid coverage ~0-5%
findings.quote: Rural Haitian boreholes are overwhelmingly NGO/donor-drilled and fitted with Afridev or India MkII HANDPUMPS because rural grid electricity is essentially absent (national electrification ~45%, rural far lower, supply intermittent). Motorized rural boreholes exist mainly as diesel- or solar-powered kiosk/piped-scheme sources. Handpump share among rural borehole users: 60-90%.
findings.motorized_split_notes: The motorized minority is diesel genset or solar (grid-independent) - for the loss-of-central-infrastructure scenario much of Haiti's motorized share SURVIVES; for HEMP it fails.
findings.caveats: Pump-count inventories, not user-weighted (pitfall 3): motorized kiosk boreholes serve more people each, so the user-weighted handpump share sits toward the lower bound. Urban Haiti (Port-au-Prince): reverse-osmosis kiosks and utility wells are motorized; urban handpump share 10-30%.

findings.source: RWSN 'History and current status of the rope pump in Nicaragua' (2022) + rope pump literature (13,000+ installed; SDC/BOMESA)
findings.quote: 'More than 13,000 rope pumps installed in Nicaragua' historically; BUT the 2022 resurvey of an original rope-pump well cohort found 'the original rope pumps in use in 20% of the wells, while... replaced by small electric centrifugal pumps in the remaining 80%.' Rural electrification (now ~99%) has converted most former handpump wells to electric. Also, rope pumps sit mostly on DUG wells (excluded category), further shrinking the handpump share within the borehole/tubewell category. -> 10-40% rural and falling.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric; solar pumping growing in dry-corridor community systems.
findings.caveats: Point evidence is one cohort resurvey; national CAPS (community water board) systems are electric pumped piped schemes. Urban: 0-10%.

findings.source: IBGE Censo 2022 / PNAD water source categories ('poco profundo ou artesiano' vs 'poco raso') + Luz para Todos rural electrification (~99.8%)
findings.quote: Brazil's census borehole category is 'poco profundo ou artesiano' - deep tubewells that by construction require motorized pumps; the shallow 'poco raso/cacimba' (dug) is a separate excluded category. Rural electrification 99.8% post-Luz para Todos; Brazil never had a handpump program at scale. Handpump share 0-8% national (residual in semi-arid Northeast and Amazonia).
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric dominant; diesel and increasingly solar in off-grid Amazonia; windmill pumps (cataventos) a small Northeast niche - technically non-electric and resilient.
findings.caveats: Denominator note: Brazil borehole users ~2-3% of population; most rural Northeast handpump-like devices are on dug wells.

findings.source: INEGI Censo 2020 water source ('pozo' category) + ~99% national electrification
findings.quote: Mexican rural 'pozo' users split dug vs drilled; drilled wells (norias vs pozos profundos) feeding households are electric-pumped; community wells are electric piped schemes. No handpump tradition at scale. 0-10% rural, 0-3% urban.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric ~100% of motorized.
findings.caveats: Census 'pozo' merges dug and drilled - the borehole-only denominator is smaller and more electric than the raw pozo row (pitfall 1/5).

findings.source: ENAPRES/Censo 2017 water categories + Amazon NGO handpump installs (small)
findings.quote: Peruvian rural non-piped water is dominated by rivers/springs/dug wells; tubewells are few. Sierra/coast boreholes are electric; scattered NGO handpump boreholes exist in Loreto/Ucayali (Amazonia, off-grid). 0-15% rural handpump share on a small denominator.
findings.motorized_split_notes: Grid-electric; solar pumping in Amazonian community systems growing.
findings.caveats: Expert bound; small stakes (<0.5M borehole users).

regional_default.rationale: For uncovered countries in Europe/CIS/MENA/LAC/high-income: (1) rural grid electrification is 95-100% nearly everywhere in this super-region, and drilled boreholes are typically deeper than the ~7-8m suction limit of cheap hand pumps, so motorized pumping is the default configuration; (2) the single direct census split found anywhere in the region (Bosnia 2013) gives manual/(manual+electric) = 1.1/(1.1+12.2) = 8.3%, sitting inside the 2-15% rural band; (3) high-income members (US EPA 23M households on private wells, Nordic bedrock boreholes, France/Austria/NZ) are effectively 0-2% handpump, pulling the urban band to 0-5%. Exceptions are carried as their own findings and should NOT use this default: Haiti (60-90% rural), lowland Central Asia - Uzbekistan/Turkmenistan Amu Darya basin (20-60% rural), Nicaragua (10-40% rural). Motorized-share composition for the default: assume ~95%+ grid-electric, diesel marginal (Yemen/Libya-style genset pumping is the main MENA deviation), solar a growing niche in off-grid and war-affected areas (Ukraine retrofits, Sahel-style solarization has little footprint in this region). Iran's ~37,000 gravity qanats are a separate resilience channel that shows up outside the borehole category.

verifications.primary_source_checked: Ukraine MICS 2012 variable WS1 via World Bank Microdata catalog 2348 (independently fetched); cross-checked with JMP WHO/UNICEF country file for Ukraine (washdata.org household download, Water Data sheet) for weighted urban/rural splits across all surveys 2000-2024; World Bank Ukraine WSS Policy Note 2021; UNICEF/IOM war reporting
verifications.evidence_quote: WS1 frequency table (catalog 2348, V305): 'Tube well, Borehole' 663 cases = 5.9%; 'Protected well' 2,432 = 21.5%; 'Piped into dwelling' 6,753 = 59.7% — matches the researcher's quote verbatim, and the variable has a single code 21 with no hand/motorized subcategory. JMP country file, UKR_2012_MICS column: tubewell/borehole = 3.1% urban, 12.2% rural, 5.6% total (weighted); UKR_2019/2021/2022_LCS rows show only 'all wells' (10.8/60.5, 10.3/55.5, 8.9/55.4 urban/rural) with no tubewell row — no post-2012 survey separates boreholes, let alone pump type. UNICEF Ukraine: 'shelling often caused power outages, disabling the pumps' (verified real quote); IOM provided six solar panel stations for borehole pumps in Mykolaiv region in 2024 (verified).
verifications.denominator_check: PASS. The claimed 5-20% (rural) and 0-5% (urban) are explicitly shares among BOREHOLE USERS, not of all households: the researcher cites the 5.9%-of-households MICS figure only as context and correctly excludes the 21.5% protected dug wells. The Bosnia analogue anchor is itself a within-well-users ratio: 1.1/(1.1+12.2) = 8.27% ~ 8.3%, arithmetic verified correct.
verifications.notes: Verdict applies to both strata claims (rural 5-20%, urban 0-5%). Every checkable element reproduced exactly: WS1 numbers, absence of pump-type split, Bosnia arithmetic, both war-reporting evidence items, and the existence of borehole users in both strata (JMP weighted: 3.1% urban / 12.2% rural of households). The handpump-share bounds themselves cannot be CONFIRMED because no Ukrainian primary source measures hand vs motorized pumping among tubewell/borehole users — MICS 2012 is the last survey with a separate tubewell category and it does not split; later LCS/SWS surveys lump all wells. Rated PLAUSIBLE, not REFUTED: the 5-20% rural range brackets the Bosnia 8.3% analogue with a defensible upward adjustment (Abyssinian driven wells and street hand-pump columns are documented Ukrainian rural phenomena), and the urban 0-5% typology claim is consistent with deep drilled wells + submersible/hydrophore practice; nothing found contradicts either range. Minor internal tension the researcher already flags in caveats: MICS-implied borehole users (~5.6-5.9% of households, roughly 2.5M-6M people) is well below the model's 11.5M, so the model category absorbs more than the MICS row; drift direction (post-2012 drilling boom = deeper + electric) correctly pushes toward the low end of the rural range. No corrected bounds proposed.
